nodes.label: Kinetic Theory of Gases
nodes.note: Kinetic theory models a gas as point molecules in random motion, turning pressure into a statistical average: $$P = \frac{1}{3}\rho \overline{v^2}$$. Degrees of freedom then fix heat capacities.

nodes.label: Gas Laws and Equation of State
nodes.group: Gas Laws and Equation of State
nodes.note: Empirical gas laws combine into the ideal gas equation $$PV = nRT$$, with $R = 8.314\ \text{J}/\text{mol}\cdot\text{K}$.

nodes.label: Boyle's Law
nodes.group: Gas Laws and Equation of State
nodes.note: At fixed temperature, pressure and volume are inverse: $$P \propto \frac{1}{V}, \ P_1V_1 = P_2V_2$$. The isotherm is a rectangular hyperbola on the P-V plane.

nodes.label: Charles's and Gay-Lussac's Laws
nodes.group: Gas Laws and Equation of State
nodes.note: At fixed pressure $V \propto T$; at fixed volume $P \propto T$: $$\frac{V_1}{T_1} = \frac{V_2}{T_2}, \ \frac{P_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2}{T_2}$$. Absolute temperature in kelvin is mandatory.

nodes.label: Combined Gas Law
nodes.group: Gas Laws and Equation of State
nodes.note: One relation covers all three variables: $$\frac{P_1V_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2V_2}{T_2}$$. It applies to a fixed mass of ideal gas between two equilibrium states.

nodes.label: Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures
nodes.group: Gas Laws and Equation of State
nodes.note: Total pressure is the sum of partial pressures of non-reacting components: $$P = p_1 + p_2 + p_3 + \dots, \ p_i = \frac{n_i}{n}P$$. Moist gas questions subtract water vapour pressure.

nodes.label: Dalton Mixture Example
nodes.group: Gas Laws and Equation of State
nodes.note: A $2\ \text{L}$ vessel holds $1\ \text{mol}$ N$_2$ and $1\ \text{mol}$ O$_2$ at $300\ \text{K}$: each partial pressure is $p_i = \frac{n_iRT}{V} \approx 12.5\ \text{atm}$, so $P \approx 25\ \text{atm}$.

nodes.label: Graham's Law of Diffusion
nodes.group: Gas Laws and Equation of State
nodes.note: Effusion rates are inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass: $$\frac{r_1}{r_2} = \sqrt{\frac{M_2}{M_1}}$$. It explains isotopic separation of uranium hexafluoride.

nodes.label: Graham Ratio Example
nodes.group: Gas Laws and Equation of State
nodes.note: He vs O$_2$: $$\frac{r_{He}}{r_{O_2}} = \sqrt{\frac{32}{4}} = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.83$$. Helium effuses nearly three times faster.

nodes.label: Avogadro's Hypothesis and Molar Volume
nodes.group: Gas Laws and Equation of State
nodes.note: Equal volumes of gases at the same $T$ and $P$ contain equal molecules: at STP one mole occupies $22.4\ \text{L}$. Density then scales as $$\rho = \frac{PM}{RT}$$.

nodes.label: Open Vessel Heating
nodes.group: Gas Laws and Equation of State
nodes.note: An open vessel at fixed $P$ and $V$ loses molecules on heating: $$\frac{n_2}{n_1} = \frac{T_1}{T_2}$$. The fraction expelled is $$1 - \frac{T_1}{T_2}$$.

nodes.label: Moist Gas Correction
nodes.group: Gas Laws and Equation of State
nodes.note: Gas collected over water contains water vapour: $$P_{gas} = P_{atm} - P_{water}$$. Vapour pressure of water depends only on temperature.

nodes.label: Kinetic Theory Postulates and Pressure
nodes.note: Ideal gas molecules are point masses with elastic collisions and no intermolecular forces. Pressure follows from momentum transfer: $$P = \frac{1}{3}\frac{N}{V}m\overline{v^2}$$.

nodes.label: Postulates of KTG
nodes.note: Molecules move randomly, collisions are perfectly elastic, and collision time is negligible. Between collisions the gas obeys Newtonian mechanics with pressure emerging statistically.

nodes.label: Kinetic Interpretation of Temperature
nodes.note: Average translational kinetic energy is proportional to absolute temperature: $$\frac{1}{2}m\overline{v^2} = \frac{3}{2}k_BT$$. This is why $T = 0\ \text{K}$ means zero kinetic energy.

nodes.label: Why Ideal Model Fails at High Density
nodes.note: At high pressure, finite molecular size and attractions matter. The van der Waals correction is $$\left(P + \frac{an^2}{V^2}\right)(V - nb) = nRT$$.

nodes.label: Collision Frequency
nodes.note: Molecules of one species collide at rate $$Z_1 = \sqrt{2}\pi d^2 n \bar{v}$$. Total intermolecular collisions per unit volume per second scale as $$Z_{11} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\pi d^2 n^2 \bar{v}$$.

nodes.label: Molecular Speeds
nodes.note: A Maxwell-Boltzmann ensemble yields three characteristic speeds: most probable, mean, and rms. Their ranking is $$v_{mp} < \bar{v} < v_{rms}$$.

nodes.label: RMS Speed
nodes.note: Root-mean-square speed is $$v_{rms} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}} = \sqrt{\frac{3k_BT}{m}}$$. It grows as $\sqrt{T}$ and falls as $\sqrt{M}$.

nodes.label: Mean and Most Probable Speeds
nodes.note: $$\bar{v} = \sqrt{\frac{8RT}{\pi M}}, \ v_{mp} = \sqrt{\frac{2RT}{M}}$$. The ratio $v_{mp} : \bar{v} : v_{rms} = 1 : 1.128 : 1.225$ is a frequent JEE ask.

nodes.label: Speed Ratio Example
nodes.note: For O$_2$ at $300\ \text{K}$, $v_{rms} = \sqrt{3RT/M} \approx 483\ \text{m}/\text{s}$, while $v_{mp} \approx 395\ \text{m}/\text{s}$.

nodes.label: Maxwell-Boltzmann Distribution
nodes.note: The speed probability density is $$f(v) = 4\pi\left(\frac{m}{2\pi k_BT}\right)^{3/2} v^2 e^{-mv^2/2k_BT}$$. Higher $T$ flattens and right-shifts the curve.

nodes.label: Mean Free Path
nodes.note: Average distance between collisions is $$\lambda = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\,\pi d^2 n} = \frac{k_BT}{\sqrt{2}\,\pi d^2 P}$$. It falls as pressure rises.

nodes.label: Temperature and Molar Mass Shift
nodes.note: The most probable speed scales as $$v_{mp} = \sqrt{\frac{2RT}{M}}$$. Heating shifts the Maxwell peak right; heavier gases shift it left.

nodes.label: Degrees of Freedom and Equipartition
nodes.note: Each quadratic energy term contributes $\frac{1}{2}k_BT$ per molecule. For $f$ degrees of freedom, $$U = \frac{f}{2}nRT$$.

nodes.label: Degrees of Freedom by Gas Type
nodes.note: Monatomic gases have $f = 3$ (translation only), diatomic have $f = 5$ at ordinary temperatures (3 translational + 2 rotational), and polyatomic have $f = 6$ with vibrations active.

nodes.label: Law of Equipartition of Energy
nodes.note: Energy is shared equally among all accessible quadratic modes: $$E_{mode} = \frac{1}{2}k_BT$$ per molecule. This explains why adding rotational modes raises heat capacity.

nodes.label: Heat Capacities and Gamma
nodes.note: Molar heats satisfy $$C_P - C_V = R, \ \gamma = \frac{C_P}{C_V} = 1 + \frac{2}{f}$$. So $\gamma = 5/3$ for monatomic and $7/5$ for diatomic gases.

nodes.label: Gas Mixtures
nodes.note: Internal energy is additive: $$U = \frac{1}{2}(n_1f_1 + n_2f_2)RT$$. Effective gamma is $$\gamma_{mix} = \frac{n_1C_{P1} + n_2C_{P2}}{n_1C_{V1} + n_2C_{V2}}$$.

nodes.label: Vibrational Modes and High-Temperature Failure
nodes.note: Vibrations add 2 degrees of freedom per mode, giving $f = 7$ classically. Quantum freezing of modes explains why measured $C_V$ falls below classical predictions at low $T$.

nodes.label: Internal Energy of Ideal Gas
nodes.note: $$U = \frac{f}{2}nRT = nC_V T$$. Since $U$ depends only on $T$, any isothermal ideal-gas process has $\Delta U = 0$.

nodes.label: Speeds in Reaction and Effusion
nodes.note: Effusion rate through a small hole is $$r = \frac{P}{\sqrt{2\pi m k_B T}}$$ per unit area. It yields Graham's law on integration over the Maxwell distribution.

nodes.label: Real Gases
nodes.note: Real gases deviate from ideality, captured by the compressibility factor $$Z = \frac{PV}{nRT}$$.

nodes.label: Compressibility Factor Z
nodes.note: $Z = 1$ marks ideality; $Z < 1$ shows attraction dominance; $Z > 1$ shows repulsion/finite size. Z vs P curves at fixed $T$ are classic graph questions.

nodes.label: Z Curve Reading
nodes.note: For H$_2$ and He, $Z > 1$ at all pressures near room temperature because repulsions dominate. For CO$_2$, $Z$ dips below 1 at moderate pressures before rising.

nodes.label: Van der Waals Equation
nodes.note: $$\left(P + \frac{an^2}{V^2}\right)(V - nb) = nRT$$ with $a$ correcting attraction and $b$ correcting volume. Both constants are material-specific.

nodes.label: Critical Constants
nodes.note: At the critical point the isotherm has an inflection: $$P_c = \frac{a}{27b^2}, \ V_c = 3b, \ T_c = \frac{8a}{27Rb}$$. Above $T_c$ no liquefaction is possible.

nodes.label: Boyle Temperature
nodes.note: At $T_B$ a real gas mimics ideal behavior over a wide pressure range: $$T_B = \frac{a}{Rb}$$. Below $T_B$ attractions dominate at low pressure.

nodes.label: Virial Equation of State
nodes.note: $$\frac{PV}{RT} = 1 + \frac{B(T)}{V} + \frac{C(T)}{V^2} + \dots$$. From van der Waals, $B(T) = b - a/(RT)$.

nodes.label: Liquefaction of Gases
nodes.note: A gas liquefies only below its critical temperature: $$T < T_c = \frac{8a}{27Rb}$$. Cooling plus compression along the Andrews isotherm produces the liquid phase.
